summary: The game has a new name, and a real front door: the world itself behind the main menu, room for as many worlds as you like, and far more of the game in your hands.

items.head: Crown Reborn.
items.text: This is the game's name from now on.

items.head: A living title screen.
items.text: The menu stands in front of your own world, drifting round the capital at dusk.

items.head: Many worlds.
items.text: Each world has its own save. Rename them, copy them, save them to a file, bring them back in, and delete them to a trash folder you can still reach.

items.head: New World choices.
items.text: Name your world, use any word as a seed, pick Gentle, Fair or Hard, start in Story or Creative, choose who waits for you, and skip heaven on a second life.

items.head: Sound, Controls, Screen and Access pages.
items.text: Separate volumes, invert mouse, toggle sprint, interface size, crosshair styles, a tidier screen, full screen, brightness, colour help, a plain font and less camera shake.

items.head: How to Play.
items.text: A short guide that always shows your own keys, on the title screen and on the pause card.

items.head: Save and quit.
items.text: The pause card can take you back to the title, and it comes back with a welcome and what you were doing.

items.head: Loading.
items.text: A real progress bar, with a tip to read.

items.head: New World no longer replaces your world.
items.text: It used to write over the only save without asking.

items.head: Two tabs cannot mix up saves.
items.text: A tab left open on one world can no longer write into another.

summary: The world is bigger, its creatures think for themselves, and something very old now sleeps under a black mountain in the east.

items.head: The Wyrm.
items.text: One dragon in all the world, asleep in a cave under the Wyrmcrown. No blade can mark it until the endgame. Wake it and it chases you off the mountain, breathing fire, and it remembers you.

items.head: A bigger world.
items.text: 10 by 10 lands, up from 8 by 8, with the drowned Mirefen in the south and two new villages.

items.head: Ten new creatures.
items.text: Deer, boars, crabs, bats, bandits, skeleton archers, cave spiders, mountain trolls and ashen wraiths, with shoals of fish in the water.

items.head: A bestiary.
items.text: The journal has an entry for every creature, unlocked the first time you get a good look at it.

items.head: More to do.
items.text: Five new guild quests, a longer board as your rank rises, more favors, and a final hunt the King offers once you are Oathbound.

items.head: Spawning like Minecraft.
items.text: Packs by biome and by light, caves with their own monsters, and lanterns that truly keep the dark things away. Nothing appears where you are looking.

items.head: Despawning that makes sense.
items.text: Creatures leave when they are far off and idle, never in front of you. Named foes track you down again.

items.head: Real pathfinding.
items.text: A shared flow field for the hunt and A* for errands, so creatures go round walls and through doors.

items.head: Smarter by nature.
items.text: Wolves encircle you, goblins run when hurt, skeletons keep their range, spiders pounce, deer bolt as a herd and guards call for help.

items.head: Grand town buildings.
items.text: The guild hall, smithy, hospital, inn, church and keep are rebuilt from the ground up, with real interiors.

items.head: Empty shops.
items.text: Blacksmiths, guild masters and doctors now keep their posts day and night, even in the middle of a big city.

items.head: Wall hopping.
items.text: Characters only jump at a one-block step, not at every wall they meet.

items.head: Lost events.
items.text: Raids, caravans and the law wait for somewhere to stand instead of quietly failing.

items.head: Not played yet.
items.text: This build has not been run through the automated tests or played in a browser, so expect rough edges, especially in the new art and the dragon fight. Old saves upgrade themselves, but the far east and south coasts will change shape.

summary: Everything that has changed since the last update on 24 October is now on main. The biggest change is how the whole world looks and moves.

items.head: New character art.
items.text: Every person and creature is redrawn as a chunky Minecraft-style skin, with mixed body types, cute elf girls, majestic kings and mermaids with long tails.

items.head: A really big dragon.
items.text: About 25 blocks across the wings. One lives in each open land of the Dragonspine Peaks and circles its lair, well away from the Law Stones.

items.head: More magic.
items.text: Frost Nova, Chain Lightning, Blink, Mana Ward and Meteor. Your mana well deepens at a temple with Mana Crystals, and slowly with every spell.

items.head: A compass.
items.text: It runs along the top of the screen and shows which way you face and where everything you are after lies.

items.head: A first-person hand.
items.text: It stays in the corner of the view and does the work: mining, punching, placing blocks and throwing spells.

items.head: Movement feels smoother.
items.text: You now speed up and slow down instead of starting and stopping dead, and the camera and creatures glide at any refresh rate.

items.head: No AI service needed.
items.text: The story, the people and every line of dialogue are written and shipped with the game, so it runs without a key.

items.head: A new interface.
items.text: Menus are now pages of one book, with a slate dock and bag for what your hands use.

items.head: Easier setup.
items.text: The README has copy-paste steps for Docker, Windows and macOS or Linux.

items.head: Ledges.
items.text: Walking up onto a one-block ledge no longer snaps you to the top instantly. The view now rises smoothly.

items.head: Flickering.
items.text: Faces and joints no longer shimmer where two surfaces overlapped.

items.head: Not tested yet.
items.text: The automated tests and a full play-through have not been run on this build, so expect some rough edges.
